subject.title: fix(baseten): reject malformed model metadata numbers

question: Should Baseten discovery accept only canonical non-exponent decimal strings, or preserve previously accepted numeric string forms until Baseten documents a stricter `/v1/models` contract?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes a provider-boundary compatibility contract, while the inspected public provider documentation describes the metadata fields but not their permitted string grammar.

options.title: Preserve accepted numeric strings pending contract proof
options.body: Keep the existing accepted finite numeric-string behavior or narrowly reject only demonstrably unsafe forms until Baseten supplies a stable lexical contract.

options.title: Adopt canonical-only strings
options.body: Accept the narrower grammar only after a provider owner confirms that exponent and whitespace-padded string values are invalid and the upgrade impact is intentional.

recommendation.title: Preserve accepted numeric strings pending contract proof
recommendation.body: Keep the existing accepted finite numeric-string behavior or narrowly reject only demonstrably unsafe forms until Baseten supplies a stable lexical contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current parser guard and can supply the provider-boundary evidence, while current-main feature ownership could not be traced in the available read-only environment.
